_comment: One voice per person, across the whole game.
The rule this file exists to keep: no two characters share a voice, even
when they are in different cases. A player who meets the same voice as two
different people stops believing the phones are different phones.
`voice_id` values are ElevenLabs ids, which is what the Magnific voiceover
endpoint takes. Every one of them was verified against the API by
generating a clip and polling it to COMPLETED — a bad id is accepted at
submit and only fails later, so a submit that returns 200 proves nothing.
`voice_registry_test.dart` fails if two speakers share an id.

elias.note: The owner. Mid-thirties, an engineer talking himself into something.

halme.note: His boss, older, shutting the conversation down. Has to sound like the room belongs to him.

maya.note: The owner. An artist recording herself at three in the morning.

brandt.note: Her manager and ex. Reasonable on the surface, which is the unpleasant part.

rui.note: The owner. Tired, talking into a stairwell, testing something that is not working.

vasco.note: In a loud bar, pleased with himself.

marta.note: Projecting to the back of a room. She is acting, and the recording only sounds like a fight.

director.note: Off in the room, not in the scene. Flat and unbothered — he is the line that gives the whole recording away.

skipped._comment: Not an oversight. Each of these is a memo that must stay silent.
skipped.s03: Every memo. Two are a boy reading aloud, and the voice library is all adults — CLAUDE.md's rule is to write the transcript and skip the clip. The other two are authored as no-speech: a street at night, and water against a canal wall.
skipped.s02.vm_010: Opens on thirty seconds of an empty room. Only the tail is spoken, and it is voiced from that point.
skipped.s04.vm_002: Forty seconds of a fridge compressor and a car going past. Nobody speaks; the recording ends on its own.
